Units will range from studios to three-bedrooms.</p><p>Also included in the project are a rooftop pool with cabanas, outdoor fire pits, fitness center, pickleball court, half-court basketball court, dog run and grooming facilities, according to Mavrek. Residents will have access to lounges, bike storage, EV charging stations and about 160 parking spaces.</p><p>The project received financing from Canadian investment firm Fengate Asset Management through its Social Opportunities Fund. The fund focuses on investments in housing, healthcare and logistics assets across the U.S. and Canada, according to the firm.</p><p>Lou Serafini, Fengate’s president and CEO, said Julep is the firm’s first U.S. real estate investment. It plans to invest in similar projects across the U.S.</p><p>“Breaking ground on Julep West Loop marks an important step in Fengate’s growth in the United States and builds on our commitment to delivering high-quality rental housing where it is needed most,” Alexander Glassman, managing director of U.S. real estate investments at Fengate, said in a news release. “With demand for housing in Chicago continuing to outpace supply, now is the time to advance well-located, mixed-use communities that connect residents to jobs, transit and amenities. Together with Mavrek, we are proud to help bring much-needed homes to the West Loop and create lasting value for residents, workers and the broader community.”</p><p>Construction is expected to take about 21 months, with first residents expected to move in early 2028.</p><p>Aldi didn't respond to a request for comment. </p><p>In response to a question about Aldi’s opening date, Mavrek reiterated that the property's first occupancy will be in 2028.</p><p>Some of Mavrek’s recent projects include the mixed-use <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/business/2022/4/18/23030627/streeterville-apartment-office-project-mavrek-development-gw-properties-luxury-living-chicago" target="_blank" ><u>Saint Grand development in Streeterville</u></a> and Portrait, a residential development in Uptown. Its other latest project, the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/small-business/2026/08/26/foxtrot-mavrek-plans-new-location-lake-view" target="_blank" ><u>Belmora</u></a> in Lake View, started pre-leasing in August.</p><p>The West Loop continues to be a magnet for new residents and development. Chicago-based developer <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/real-estate/2024/07/16/lg-group-fulton-market-development-apartment-grocery-plan-commission" target="_blank" ><u>LG Group</u></a> is planning to build two towers — one at 170 N. May St. and another at 175 N. Racine Ave. — in the West Loop. In January, Skokie-based F&F Realty proposed converting the eight-story building at 1060 W. Van Buren St. into apartments, while adding a <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/real-estate/2026/01/08/apartments-proposed-at-west-loop-industrial-site" >27-story tower</a> with more apartments next door.</p><p>The United Center's 1901 Project is also expected to greatly impact the West Loop with new housing, retail and hospitality. Phase 1, which broke ground in June, will be anchored by a <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/real-estate/2025/02/18/united-center-first-phase-1901-redevelopment-chicago-zoning-committee" target="_blank" ><u>6,000-seat music hall</u></a> and include a 180-room hotel, retail space and two parking garages.</p><p>“The West Loop has become one of Chicago's most in-demand neighborhoods, and we're honored to support the continued growth of the area by delivering much-needed housing anchored by one of the world’s most reputable grocers,” Anthony Hrusovsky, partner and chief investment officer at Mavrek, said.</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/real-estate/2024/10/25/aldi-open-first-west-loop-store-amid-large-scale-expansion-plans" >Aldi to open first West Loop store as it continues broader expansion plans</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p>

entries.title: Who will call Bears games on Fox, CBS this season? Here are my annual predictions
entries.summary: <p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" >Bears</a> aren’t the NFL’s TV darlings yet, but they’re certainly auditioning to be.</p><p>Since drafting quarterback Caleb Wiliams with the first pick in the 2024 draft, the Bears’ national-TV exposure slowly but surely has increased. They had three prime-time games in Williams’ rookie season and four last season. They’re scheduled for five this season.</p><p>But the NFL doesn’t just look at night games. On the whole, it tracks stand-alone games. With more outlets airing games in more windows, the league has more chances to show its best teams. The NFL has the Bears playing in seven such games across six outlets — ABC, CBS, ESPN, NBC, Netflix and Prime. That’s two more stand-alone games than they had in 2024 and 2025.</p><p>The Bears also have two appearances in the NFL’s most-viewed window, 3:25 p.m. Sunday, both on Fox. That’s up from one last season and none the season before. And those five night games include a stretch of three in a row from Week 7 to 9. The nation will get its fill of the Bears.</p><p>It also will get some new broadcast teams. After putting <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/sports-media/2026/09/01/tony-romo-pleads-no-contest-to-operating-while-intoxicated" >top analyst Tony Romo on leave</a> because of his drunk-driving charge, CBS moved J.J. Watt from the second team to join Jim Nantz. Ross Tucker replaced Watt alongside Ian Eagle. Since being taken over by ESPN, NFL Network has new crews, as well as, but the Bears won’t appear there.</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/sports-media/2026/09/04/tony-romo-cbs-sports-nfl-david-berson-jim-nantz-jj-watt-ian-eagle-owi-dui-al-michaels-nbc-sports" >Tony Romo vs. CBS might be best game this NFL season that no one sees</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p>What follows is my annual, fruitless attempt to predict which crews will call each Bears game. Crews for Sunday afternoons in Weeks 1-2 have been set, and we know the national crews. The rest are based on intuition and preference.</p><p><b>Week 1: at Panthers, noon, Fox —</b> Bulls TV voice Adam Amin, analyst Drew Brees and sideline reporter Kristina Pink will call it.</p><p><b>Week 2: vs. Vikings, noon, Fox —</b> Joe Davis, Greg Olsen and Pam Oliver have the call.</p><p><b>Week 3: vs. Eagles, 7:15 p.m., ESPN/ABC —</b> The “Monday Night Football” crew of Joe Buck, Troy Aikman and reporters Lisa Salters and Laura Rutledge will call it.</p><p><b>Week 4: vs. Jets, noon, Fox —</b> The Cowboys, Packers and Rams also play on Fox this week. A New York-Chicago game is perfect for Kenny Albert, former Jets LB Jonathan Vilma and Megan Olivi.</p><p><b>Week 5: at Packers, 3:25 p.m., Fox — </b> The “America’s Game of the Week” crew of Kevin Burkhardt, Tom Brady, Erin Andrews and Tom Rinaldi has the call.</p><p><b>Week 6: at Falcons, noon, Fox —</b> A soft slate sends the No. 2 crew to Atlanta, but it won’t include Davis, who’ll be away calling the MLB postseason. Fox has yet to announce his fill-in.</p><p><b>Week 7: vs. Patriots, 7:15 p.m., Prime — </b> Al Michaels, Kirk Herbstreit and Kaylee Hartung have the call.</p><p><b>Week 8: at Seahawks, 7:15 p.m., ESPN —</b> Not only will Bears fans get Buck and Aikman, they’ll get <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/09/08/bears-coach-ben-johnson-peyton-eli-manning-cast-plays-security-guard-video-nfl" >the Manning brothers.</a> “Monday Night Football with Peyton and Eli” will air on ESPN2.</p><p><b>Week 9: vs. Buccaneers, 7:20 p.m., NBC 5 —</b> Mike Tirico, Cris Collinsworth and Melissa Stark will call it.</p><p><b>Week 10:</b> Bye</p><p><b>Week 11: vs. Saints, noon, Fox —</b> Fox also has the Bills and Cowboys. Sounds like a good fit for Amin, who surely will enjoy a home game. Then he can call Cavaliers-Bulls on Monday.</p><p><b>Week 12: at Lions, noon, CBS —</b> Jim Nantz, J.J. Watt and Tracy Wolfson get their first look at the Bears on Thanksgiving.</p><p><b>Week 13: vs. Jaguars, noon, Fox —</b> The Jaguars got a lot of fifth and sixth crews last season — and the team was good! That brings Kevin Kugler, Daryl Johnston and Allison Williams to town.</p><p><b>Week 14: at Dolphins, noon, CBS —</b> Not a great week for CBS, but Bears fans will have a great week listening to the dulcet tones of Kevin Harlan with Trent Green and Melanie Collins.</p><p><b>Week 15: at Bills, 7:20 p.m., CBS —</b> A Saturday night on CBS brings Nantz and Watt to town.</p><p><b>Week 16: vs. Packers, noon, Netflix — </b> The streamer has a Christmas doubleheader. The top crew of Noah Eagle, Luke Kuechly and reporters Tom Pelissero and MJ Acosta-Ruiz should call Game 1.</p><p><b>Week 17: vs. Lions, 3:25 p.m., Fox — </b> Burkhardt and Brady make their first Chicago appearance this season. Will they return in the postseason?</p><p><b>Week 18: at Vikings, TBD, TBD —</b> With so many stand-alone games, this game appears to be the only one that could be flexed into prime time. Of course, both teams need to be good.</p><h3>Remote patrol</h3><p>After the “Hail Mary” travesty last week, beginning Saturday, all football broadcasts from Big Ten venues that include conference replay and on-field officials will be able to supplement the video during reviews with live audio between the referee and replay official.</p><p>• The Score midday co-host <b>Mark Grote</b> will host the station’s Bears pregame and postgame shows to start the season, alongside analysts <b>Olin Kreutz</b> and <b>Patrick Mannelly</b>. <b>Zach Zaidman</b>, who’s part of The Score’s Cubs broadcasts, will take over for Grote after baseball season.</p><p>• NBC 5 will launch “Tonight with <b>Lou Canellis</b>,” a live, half-hour weeknight show about sports, entertainment and pop culture, at 6:30 p.m. Monday. Contributors will include former Bears coach <b>Dave Wannstedt</b>. Friday shows will be hosted by The Score’s <b>Laurence Holmes</b>.</p><h3>NFL TV crews</h3><p><b>CBS</b></p><p>Jim Nantz, J.J. Watt, Tracy Wolfson</p><p>Ian Eagle, Ross Tucker, Evan Washburn</p><p>Kevin Harlan, Trent Green, Melanie Collins</p><p>Andrew Catalon, Logan Ryan, A.J. Ross</p><p>Spero Dedes, Adam Archuleta, Aditi Kinkhabwala</p><p>Tom McCarthy, Robert Turbin, Tiffany Blackmon</p><p><b>FOX</b></p><p>Kevin Burkhardt, Tom Brady, Erin Andrews, Tom Rinaldi</p><p>Joe Davis, Greg Olsen, Pam Oliver</p><p>Adam Amin, Drew Brees, Kristina Pink</p><p>Kenny Albert, Jonathan Vilma, Megan Olivi</p><p>Kevin Kugler, Daryl Johnston, Allison Williams</p><p>Chris Myers, Mark Schlereth, Jen Hale</p>

entries.title: The Bears' pass-catchers might be the best they've had in 13 years
entries.summary: <p>When the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a>’ pass-catchers were done with their throwing session at USC this spring, Caleb Williams invited them out to dinner.</p><p>They went to The Bird Streets Club, a private club of which Williams is a member, on the Sunset Strip in West Hollywood. When dinner was finished, they walked downstairs into a private room, where the quarterback had arranged for the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/halas-intrigue/2026/09/10/bears-panthers-predictions-podcast" target="_blank" >Bears</a>’ passing highlights to be played on a loop from a big-screen television.</p><p>Williams and his pass catchers relived all their completions last year, from the mundane to the amazing. When tight end Colston Loveland caught the 58-yard touchdown pass that eventually beat the Bengals, they marveled at the play — and head coach Ben Johnson sprinting down the sideline.</p><p>There were years when the Bears’ passing clips wouldn’t have lasted very long — or have been very fun to watch. This year, the Bears hope the highlight reel grows even longer.</p><p>Williams has the weapons to do it, with a better roster of pass-catchers than either Mitch Trubisky or Justin Fields ever had. They have a chance to be the Bears’ best pass-catching group since the 2013 team that boasted wideouts Alshon Jeffrey (1,421 receiving yards) and Brandon Marshall (1,295), tight end Martellus Bennett (759) and running back Matt Forte (594).</p><p>If receiver Luther Burden and tight end Colston Loveland make the leap many inside Halas Hall believe they will in Year 2 — and if the Bears stay healthy — this year’s group should trump last season’s.</p><p>“So much talent … ” Loveland said after Thursday’s practice. “Just so versatile, so many guys that can do a bunch of different things. That obviously benefits us a lot. And there’s so many weapons, it’s going to be tough for defenses to figure out what they want to do.”</p><p>Their health got more complicated a week ago, when receiver Rome Odunze walked off the practice field during a walk-through with a right calf injury. He was limited in Thursday’s practice report for the second-straight day. Friday’s practice should go a long way toward forecasting his availability in Sunday’s opener against the Panthers. Odunze missed five games last year and was hampered in more with chronic foot issues.</p><p>Burden, who hurt his groin during training camp, and rookie receiver Zavion Thomas, who hurt his knee around the same time, are both absent from the injury report. Throw in receivers Kalif Raymond and Jahdae Walker, tight ends Cole Kmet and Sam Roush, and running backs D’Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai, and there will be no shortage of targets. The Bears' pass catchers are a basketball team, with small, quick players as well as explosive leapers and big bodies.</p><p>The Bears signed Raymond and drafted Thomas as part of their push to add speed; at one point during training camp, the Bears tracked seven receivers running at least 21 mph during practice.</p><p>“The first thing I see is speed, as far as guys rolling downfield, running up on cats, making them back up … “ quarterbacks coach J.T. Barrett said. “I tell them all the time, we’ve got, like, prototype tight ends — thoroughbreds as they're running downfield.”</p><p>Johnson notoriously said he wanted to buy Burden stock. Burden, meanwhile, predicted big things for Loveland.</p><p>“I see a breakout year,” Burden said.</p><p>Each player’s usage will vary from week-to-week. Johnson — and, by extension, Williams — will have options.</p><p>“It's up to them who's going to be in on this many plays. …” Williams said. “You've got to block. You've got to run off the ball. You've got to do your job. You've got to know where you are. You've got to know where you need to line up. And so, I think, like I said, it's up to them. And we've got some good guys out there.”</p>
